beats.spoken: Every cream in the EU comes with a file you'll never get to see.

It's called the product information file. Under Article 11 of the EU cosmetics regulation, the responsible person keeps one for every product placed on the market. The description has to link the file clearly to its product.

It holds five things: a description of the product, the safety report, the manufacturing method with a statement on good manufacturing practice, proof of the claimed effect where needed, and data on any animal testing.
And the file sticks around. It's kept for ten years, counted from the date the last batch of the product was placed on the market.

nodes.text: the last batch is placed on the market
that's how long the file stays

beats.spoken: In the US, the MoCRA law of 2022 requires something similar. The responsible person has to keep records that support the safety of their products. The law there doesn't prescribe specific tests, but it does require adequate evidence.
The file is kept at the address on the label, ready for the authorities. So that address on your pack is more than a formality: it shows where the paperwork for the product lives.
